messages:
Kevin (Sales): Heads-up — RetailCorp asked for a Private/VPC pod estimate for their holiday spike (Nov–Dec). They expect a 6x baseline traffic bump, ~1.8M requests/day peak, median request ~120 tokens, 95th latency target 250ms. Can we quick-scan GPU hours and procurement constraints?

Maya (eng-infra): Quick note: baseline traffic today?

Kevin (Sales): Their current hosted usage maps to ~300k requests/day right now, so peak ~1.8M = 6x. They want ~40% headroom above expected peak.

Tom (eng-sre): Ok. Rough capacity calc: assume model is 70 tokens/sec per A100-80GB (gen-style baseline) at p95 with our optimized runtime. For 120 tokens/request -> ~1.7 requests/sec per GPU if no batching. With batching & 50% effective batching uplift -> ~2.6 rps/GPU.

Priya (eng-platform): I usually use this formula: GPUs_needed = ceil((peak_rps * (1+headroom)) / effective_rps_per_gpu).

Maya (eng-infra): Let's plug numbers quickly: peak_rps = 1.8M / 86400 ≈ 20.83 rps. With 40% headroom -> 29.16 rps. Effective_rps_per_gpu ~2.6 → GPUs ≈ 11.22 → round up to 12 GPUs.

Tom (eng-sre): So ~12 high-memory GPUs (A100/A800 class). That translates to ~1 full rack (8 GPUs) + 1 half-rack depending on chassis. Expect ~2U vs 4U differences. For on-prem quoting use 12 GPUs across 2 chassis for N+1 layout → plan for 15 total (12 + 1 spare chassis GPU capacity) to tolerate a node failure.

Priya (eng-platform): GPU-hours: 12 GPUs * 24h * 30d ≈ 8,640 GPU-hours/month (no maintenance). With N+1 spare (15 provisioned) you pay for 15 * 24 * 30 = 10,800 GPU-hours worth of capacity to reserve.

Maya (eng-infra): Procurement lead time: for A800/A100 sku from major vendor estimate 8–12 weeks QTD; for certain suppliers up to 16. If customer needs gear before Oct, we should start procurement by early Jul at the latest.

Kevin (Sales): They asked about cost delta for 4-bit quantized variant we can recommend.

Tom (eng-sre): With 4-bit quantization and kernel optimizations, effective_rps_per_gpu can improve ~1.8x-ish (depends on model). If we assume 1.7x, effective_rps_per_gpu -> 4.4 rps. GPUs needed → ceil(29.16 / 4.4) ≈ 7 GPUs. With N+1 reserve -> 8 GPUs provisioned. Big saving on hardware and power. Tradeoff: we need to validate accuracy regressions with their eval set.

Priya (eng-platform): Also consider caching/prefixing — RetailCorp product catalog is stable for subsets. If we add prefix KV cache for product-description tokens, effective token work per request drops ~20–30% on average -> fewer GPUs. Recommend a combined approach: quantize + caching + tuned batching.

Maya (eng-infra): Networking: plan for 2x25GbE NICs per server (40Gb+ recommended if using large scorer pipelines). Egress between customer VPC and redundant DCs: if they want cross-region DR, double the inter-region bandwidth and we need async model/kv replication.

Tom (eng-sre): Operational SLOs: target p95 < 250ms. Add autoscaling buffer for sustained >70% GPU utilization triggers to avoid queuing. For Private deploy we can bake in burst doors to Dedicated hosted pool as fallback — requires contract.

capacity-bot: NOTE: Suggested GPU SKU list attached: [A800-80GB, A100-80GB, H100 (validate compatibility)]. Estimated power draw per GPU node: 3.2–4.0 kW per rack.

Kevin (Sales): Client also asked about seasonal short-term bursts instead of full commit. Can we recommend a hybrid: reserve baseline on-prem + short-term Dedicated burst?

Priya (eng-platform): Yes. Hybrid looks good: reserve 6 GPUs on-prem (steady baseline), configure routing policy to route overflow to Dedicated. If we assume baseline 300k/day -> baseline_rps ~3.47 rps -> with 40% headroom ~4.86 rps → fits on 2 GPUs (quantized) or 3 GPUs (fp). So reserve ~6 for buffer + 4–6 on Dedicated for holiday peak bursts. That reduces capital and limits procurement timing pressure.

Maya (eng-infra): TL;DR action items: 1) Confirm model family & whether quantization acceptable (Sales + ML). 2) Decide on pure capex vs hybrid burst (Sales + Customer). 3) Start procurement leadtime if pure on-prem (target PO by 2026-07-05). 4) Plan N+1 topology and network NIC reqs.

Kevin (Sales): I'll loop in RetailCorp PM and ML lead. Quick ask — can we produce a 1-page hardware + cost summary by EOD Friday?

Tom (eng-sre): I can draft the GPU-hour calc + N+1 layout. Maya will add procurement notes. Priya will add routing/fallback config.

Priya (eng-platform): I'll draft the 1-pager and include fallback playbook for Dedicated burst and telemetry keys to monitor (token-cost, p95 latency, batch size distribution).

Kevin (Sales): Great — thanks team. :thumbsup:

Maya (eng-infra): Also: flag for procurement — vendor lead times vary, consider short-term rental for any gap. :warning:

capacity-bot: ACTION: created ticket INF-7842 for procurement timeline & rental vendor eval.
